name: Better Auth
summary: Better Auth is a free, open-source code library you install and run yourself to add login to your app, instead of using a hosted service.

free_plan_covers.note: The core library is free open source with no user limits; you self-host it and only pay for your own database and hosting.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No plan is required to use the library. An optional managed Infrastructure add-on with a dashboard and audit logs costs $20/month.

portability.note: It stores users and sessions as plain tables in your own database, using standard sessions instead of a vendor-hosted store.

mobile_sdk.note: An official Expo plugin handles secure token storage and deep-link sign-in for React Native apps.

prebuilt_ui.note: The library is headless by design and ships no screens; a separate community project offers optional UI components.

builtin_email_production_ready.note: Better Auth sends no email itself; you must implement sendVerificationEmail and sendResetPassword using your own email provider.

setup.step: Install the better-auth package in your Next.js project.
Create a server-side auth config file that connects Better Auth to your own database.
Set a random secret and your app's URL in your environment file, alongside your own database connection variable.
Run Better Auth's CLI to create the needed tables in your database.
Add the Next.js route handler and create a client for use in your components.

builder_notes: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is required; without a strong random value, authentication will not work correctly.
Requires a real database connection since Better Auth stores users and sessions in your own database, not a hosted one.
Run the CLI's generate or migrate command before first use, or the required auth tables will not exist yet.
